question: Patients chosen because one cholesterol reading was high are retested a week later, untreated. What will their average be?
answer: Lower. Any single reading is a person's usual level plus day-to-day variation and lab error. Choosing people for one high reading picks many caught on a high day, and their next result drifts back. Barnett and colleagues show that drift can pass for a treatment effect in any study that recruits on one measurement.
move: Anyone picked for an extreme will look more ordinary the next time.
trap: About the same, since nothing was done to change it.
source: Barnett et al., Int J Epidemiology, 2005
reference: Barnett, van der Pols & Dobson, Regression to the mean: what it is and how to deal with it, International Journal of Epidemiology, 2005
